title: Algebra
summary: Around 820 in Baghdad, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi wrote a treatise whose title gives us the word algebra, and which MacTutor considers the first book written on the subject. It solves linear and quadratic equations, and he says it was meant for what people need in inheritance, trade and measuring land. He worked at the House of Wisdom under Caliph al-Mamun.

uncertainty.note: Al-Khwarizmi composed his algebra treatise during the reign of Caliph al-Ma'mun (813–833 CE); historians of mathematics conventionally date the work to around 820 CE.

as_recorded.value: from about 820 written by Muhammad Al-Khwarizmi

importance.justification: Al-Khwarizmi's treatise founded algebra as an autonomous discipline, introducing systematic methods for equation-solving that became the foundational language of global science, engineering, and computation.
